# Design rules

Every number the pipeline uses. *Provenance / validation* shows the strongest evidence for each rule (see docs/PLAN.md section 7). Sources and exact quotes are in the YAML files.

## `rules/color.yaml`

| Rule | Summary | Default | Range | Unit | Kind | Provenance / validation | Applies to | Conditions and notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color.edges.furry_sigma_px` | Gaussian blur (in image pixels) applied to each color's indicator before every pixel takes the color with the largest blurred value, for the `furry` edge preset. Less blur than `smooth`, so more of the image's jagged edge detail is kept. | 1 |  | px | hypothesis | unverified / untested | C2 | Set in pixels, like flat.smooth.sigma_px, because the jaggedness comes from the image. Detail finer than about one bead width (0.42 mm) does not print; it merges or vanishes in the slicer. So furry means less smoothing and sharper corners, not hair-fine strands. |
| `color.extract.default_count` | How many colors quantize extracts before outline handling and merges, when the config does not say (the `extract` setting). The final palette is then reduced to at most `colors` by the owner's merges and the outline handling. | 6 |  | count | hypothesis | primary / untested | C2 | A count of palette colors, not a print threshold. When extract is not given, it defaults to the larger of this value and `colors` (tdmg.color_config), so the default never falls below the final palette's maximum; an extract given in a flag or the config file is never raised and is refused if below `colors`. This replaces the plan's earlier idea (Task 7b's first draft) of deriving the count as colors + merges + 1. At most `colors` survive into the final palette; if more remain, the plan is written with ready false. Larger values split Roadie's outline into more fringe clusters (the record's Surprises). |
| `color.outline.thin_share` | An extracted color is in the outline family when more than this share of its pixels is removed by the printable opening (width flat.sliver.opening_width), i.e. when it is mostly thin lines. Used by `outline_color: auto`. | 0.38 | 0–1 | fraction | hypothesis | primary / untested | C2 | A share of pixels (0 to 1), not a length. It depends on the opening width and the scale (mm per pixel), so the same image at another print width can give other shares. Two images only. |
| `color.shade.max_hue_diff_deg` | After the outline family is removed, two extracted colors are flagged as a likely shade pair when their CIELAB hue angles differ by less than this. Flags are reported for the owner, never applied. | 5.5 | 0–180 | deg | hypothesis | primary / untested | C2 | Applies only to pairs where both colors pass color.shade.min_chroma (a near-grey color's hue angle means nothing). Two images and one counterexample. |
| `color.shade.min_chroma` | A color takes part in shade-pair flags only if its CIELAB chroma C* is above this, so white, grey and black, whose hue angle is meaningless, are never flagged by hue. | 8.5 |  | cielab_chroma | hypothesis | primary / untested | C2 | CIELAB chroma, sqrt(a*^2 + b*^2), D65 white (tdmg.color.srgb_to_lab). Not a separator of outlines from shade pairs; the record shows no chroma floor does that, which is why the outline family is removed first. |
| `color.outline.keep_width` | Default width of the band that `outlines: keep` draws in the darkest outline-family color: it redraws the drawing's own lines (the ridge of the family's thin strokes) and runs inside the outer edge. The config key outline_width_mm overrides it. | 0.5 |  | mm | hypothesis | primary / untested | C2 | absolute: does not scale with the model; In mm, not pixels, because it is a printed width. It must stay above flat.sliver.opening_width (0.4 mm) or cleanup removes the band; tests/test_rules.py checks that it does, and tdmg.color_config refuses an outline_width_mm at or below it. Close above the opening is not enough: at 0.45 mm (less than one pixel above it on the owner's images) cleanup removed up to 28.6% of the band. History: 0.6 mm (Task 7c, a round starting value); 0.45 mm (Task 7e-b, our reading of the owner's "0.4 mm?", since 0.4 mm equals the opening and cannot be used); 0.5 mm (after the measurement). Two images at 60 mm only; at other scales the margin over the opening in pixels changes. Whether a 0.5 mm band (about one 0.42 mm bead) prints cleanly is untested. |
| `color.outline.keep_area_width_ratio` | When the outline family is dropped, a wide area of the core color (a 4-connected component of the core's pixels that its own opening keeps) stays in the core color only if its inscribed width (2 x the largest distance from its pixels to the nearest pixel outside it) is at least this many times the family's stroke width (the 90th percentile of 2 x that distance on the ridge of the family's thin strokes). Other wide areas take the nearest non-family color. | 2 |  | ratio | hypothesis | primary / untested | C2 | A ratio of two widths, so it does not depend on the print width or the image's resolution, unlike a width in mm (the 7e-a record notes that at 120 mm a fixed 1.25 mm threshold would sit close to Roadie's strokes). The 7e-a widths were measured on components of the union of all members' wide pixels; the rule measures components of the core's own wide pixels, which are subsets of those, so their widths are no larger. The width is read on the pixel grid (about 1 px above the true width). With no family stroke, no wide area is kept. One positive example, Roadie's pupil; nothing else supports the value. |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `format.3mf.edge_manifold` | Every triangle edge is shared with exactly one other triangle (no holes, no non-manifold edges). | yes |  | bool | normative | primary / untested | all | object_type = model or solidsupport; An edge rule only. Two solids touching at a single vertex pass it (and pass lib3mf's IsManifoldAndOriented); see gate.topology.vertex_manifold. |
| `format.3mf.consistent_orientation` | Adjacent triangles have the same face-normal orientation, and all normals point outward. | yes |  | bool | normative | primary / untested | all | object_type = model or solidsupport |
| `format.3mf.self_intersection_is_warning` | Self-intersections are a warning, not a format violation; consumers must accept them. | yes |  | bool | normative | primary / untested | all |  |
| `gate.topology.vertex_manifold` | Require every vertex to be manifold (no two surfaces pinched together at a single point). | yes |  | bool | hypothesis | primary / untested | all | Not required by 3MF. Checked locally 2026-11-09 - two cubes sharing one vertex pass trimesh is_watertight and lib3mf IsManifoldAndOriented, so this needs its own check (for example Open3D is_vertex_manifold). |

| `flat.smooth.sigma_px` | Gaussian blur (in image pixels) applied to the binary mask before taking its 0.5 iso-contour, to smooth jagged outlines of soft or low-resolution images. | 2.5 |  | px | hypothesis | primary / untested | G1 | Set in pixels because the jaggedness comes from image resolution and compression, not print size.
